Motivating with AI

Hands-On Techniques for the Classroom  ·  Prof. Galyna Lutsenko

1 / 16
Station A & Station B
Complete A individually first (5 min), then B as a full table (5 min).
Station A · 5 min · individual

Instant Feedback

Write 3–5 sentences explaining a concept from your subject. Paste into AI with this prompt:

PROMPT
"Give me feedback on this explanation as if you are a secondary school student who finds this topic genuinely hard. Be honest — tell me what is unclear, what is missing, and what helped."

RTF breakdown:
R: "a secondary school student…" · T: "give me feedback" · F: "be honest, tell me what is unclear / missing / helpful"

Notice: Did the feedback change your wording — or your thinking?

Station B · 5 min · full table

Socratic Dialogue — Team Socrates

One person types — everyone decides what to answer together (20–30 sec per turn). Rotate the typist every 2 rounds. Run 5–6 turns.

PROMPT
"You are a Socratic tutor. Ask us questions — do not give answers — to help us understand [topic]. Keep asking until we arrive at the key insight ourselves. Start with the first question now."

You are a Socratic tutor. Ask us questions — do not give answers — to help us understand [topic]. Keep asking until we arrive at the key insight ourselves. Start with the first question now.

Suggested topics:
☐ Why do students forget what they learned?
☐ What makes an explanation clear?
☐ When does a student actually need a teacher?

Notice: Which question stopped the group for a moment?

Technique Gallery
Six techniques · one per table · use with your chosen situation.
Table 1

⚔ Debate Partner

AI as: an Opponent
Supports: Autonomy & Competence
Notice: Did AI change your argument?
PROMPT
"I am going to share a position about [your situation]. Take the opposite view. Challenge every argument I make with evidence and counter-questions. Do not agree with me, even if my point is good. Start by stating your position clearly."
Table 2

🎭 Role Play

AI as: a Character
Supports: Relatedness & Autonomy
Notice: What did AI reveal that surprised you?
PROMPT
"Act as [a person connected to your situation]. Be realistic — show their inner state, not just behaviour. Respond to what I say and ask me questions back. Stay in character throughout."
Table 3

🔍 Error Detective

AI as: an Imperfect Expert
Supports: Competence & Relatedness
Notice: Was it easier to learn through errors?
PROMPT
"Write a short explanation (6–8 sentences) of [a concept related to your situation]. Deliberately include three factual or logical mistakes. Do not tell me where they are."
Table 4

🪞 Reflection Coach

AI as: a Thinking Partner
Supports: Autonomy & Competence
Notice: Which question shifted your thinking most?
PROMPT
"Act as a reflection coach. I am dealing with [briefly describe your situation]. Ask me one question at a time — not to evaluate or advise — only to help me think more clearly about what is happening and what I can influence. Start now."
Table 5

✍ Creative Co-author

AI as: a Co-creator
Supports: Autonomy & Competence
Notice: Where did AI take the piece unexpectedly?
PROMPT
"We are going to write a short [scenario / reflective piece / argument] together about [your situation]. We alternate: I write two sentences, you continue with two — adding something new or unexpected each time. Do not repeat what I wrote. Push the thinking further. I will start."
Table 6

🎲 Scenario Generator

AI as: a Case Designer
Supports: Competence & Relatedness
Notice: How does seeing multiple versions change your response?
PROMPT
"Generate three different versions of this situation: [your chosen situation]. Each version should have a different underlying cause, a different context, and one thing not immediately visible that explains what is really going on. Make each realistic and distinct."
RTF — Quick Start
Three questions. One prompt.
R
Role
Who will AI be?
a Socratic tutor · a confused student · a critical reviewer · a historical figure
T
Task
What will AI do?
give feedback · ask questions · generate cases · co-write · find errors
F
Format
How should AI respond?
one question at a time · honest and direct · in character · bullet points
PARTS — Student Prompt Design
RTF gets you started. PARTS gets you there.
P
Purpose
Why is the student doing this?
What is the learning goal of this AI interaction?
A
Audience
Who is the AI speaking to?
What does it need to know about the student to respond well?
R
Role
Who will AI be?
Tutor · coach · critic · confused student · character
T
Task
What specifically will AI do?
Feedback · questioning · co-writing · generating cases
S
Style
How should AI respond?
Tone · length · format · level of formality
Example — Reflection Coach prompt using PARTS

P: help student reflect after difficult feedback  ·  A: a student who feels like giving up
R: reflection coach  ·  T: ask one question at a time, no advice  ·  S: calm, non-judgmental

FULL PROMPT
"Act as a reflection coach. I have just received difficult feedback and feel like giving up. Ask me one question at a time — not to evaluate or advise, only to help me think clearly about what I can control. Start now."
